name: Retatrutide
use: Triple agonist (GLP-1/GIP/glucagon) used for obesity and type 2 diabetes.
vial: 10 mg lyophilized; commonly reconstituted in 1 mL to 10 mg/mL
doseRange: 1–12 mg once weekly, usually started at 1 or 2 mg and increased.
evidence: Human clinical trials (phase 2 published; phase 3 ongoing). Not TGA or FDA approved.
disclaimer: Human clinical trials (phase 2 published; phase 3 ongoing). Not TGA or FDA approved. Typical dose figures are from phase 2 trials.

name: Wolverine (BPC-157 + TB-500)
use: Blend of BPC-157 and TB-500, used for recovery and tissue repair.
vial: Commonly 5 mg + 5 mg or 10 mg + 10 mg lyophilized; reconstitution varies by vial
doseRange: BPC-157 250–500 mcg once or twice daily, and TB-500 2–5 mg twice weekly.
frequency: Often a daily BPC-157 component and a twice-weekly TB-500 component.
evidence: No human trial data for the blend; figures are commonly cited research-use only.
disclaimer: No human trial data for the blend. Figures are commonly cited research-use only and follow the component peptides: BPC-157 250–500 mcg once or twice daily, and TB-500 2–5 mg twice weekly.

name: KCU
use: Skin and tissue repair (GHK-Cu or a GHK-Cu/KPV blend).
vial: Vial size depends on what the name refers to; GHK-Cu is often 50 mg, KPV often 5–10 mg
doseRange: If GHK-Cu, 1–2 mg daily; if the blend includes KPV, 200–500 mcg daily of KPV.
evidence: No standardised product or human trial protocol under this name. See also GHK-Cu and KPV.
disclaimer: KCU is not a standardised product, and there is no human trial protocol under this name. It may refer to GHK-Cu or a GHK-Cu/KPV blend; dosing depends on which peptide is in the vial. See also GHK-Cu and KPV.

name: BPC-157
use: Used for tissue and gut repair.
vial: 5 mg or 10 mg lyophilized; often 5 mg in 2 mL (2.5 mg/mL) so 250 mcg is 0.1 mL
doseRange: 250–500 mcg once or twice daily (subcutaneous).
evidence: No robust human trial data; figures are commonly cited research-use only.
disclaimer: No robust human trial data; figures are commonly cited research-use only.

name: TB-500
use: Thymosin beta-4 fragment, used for recovery and injury repair.
vial: 5 mg or 10 mg lyophilized; often 5 mg in 2 mL (2.5 mg/mL)
doseRange: 2–5 mg twice weekly for a loading phase, then often 2 mg weekly or fortnightly.
frequency: Twice weekly, then a lower weekly or fortnightly maintenance dose
evidence: Limited human data (some thymosin beta-4 wound-healing studies); figures are commonly cited research-use.
disclaimer: Limited human data (some thymosin beta-4 wound-healing studies); figures are commonly cited research-use.

name: CJC-1295
use: GHRH analogue used to raise growth-hormone release.
vial: 2 mg or 5 mg lyophilized; often 2 mg in 2 mL (1 mg/mL) so 100 mcg is 0.1 mL
doseRange: Without DAC (Mod GRF 1-29): 100–300 mcg 1–3 times daily. With DAC: 1–2 mg once or twice weekly.
frequency: 1–3 times daily (no DAC) or once or twice weekly (with DAC)
evidence: Some human data, mainly for the DAC form. Confirm whether a vial includes DAC, because dosing differs.
disclaimer: Some human data exist, mainly for the DAC form. Confirm whether a vial includes DAC, because dosing differs.

name: Ipamorelin
use: Growth-hormone secretagogue (ghrelin receptor agonist).
vial: 2 mg or 5 mg lyophilized; often 2 mg in 2 mL (1 mg/mL) so 200 mcg is 0.2 mL
doseRange: 200–300 mcg 1–3 times daily, often at bedtime.
evidence: Some human studies exist (including ghrelin-agonist research). Common subcutaneous figures are from research and practitioner use.
disclaimer: Some human studies exist (including ghrelin-agonist research). Common subcutaneous figures are from research and practitioner use.

name: CJC-1295 / Ipamorelin
use: Combined GH-secretagogue blend (usually CJC-1295 without DAC plus ipamorelin).
vial: Commonly 2 mg CJC-1295 (no DAC) + 2 mg ipamorelin, reconstituted in 2 mL so 100 mcg of each is 0.1 mL
doseRange: 100–300 mcg of each, 1–2 times daily (no-DAC CJC).
evidence: Limited formal trial data for the combination; figures are commonly cited research-use.
disclaimer: Limited formal trial data for the combination; figures are commonly cited research-use.

name: Tesamorelin
use: GHRH analogue used to reduce visceral fat in HIV-associated lipodystrophy.
vial: 1 mg or 2 mg vials (approved product reconstitution is specific to the brand)
doseRange: 2 mg once daily.
evidence: FDA-approved product and dose for a specific indication.
disclaimer: FDA-approved product and dose for HIV-associated lipodystrophy, a specific indication.

name: MOTS-c
use: Mitochondrial-derived peptide used for metabolic health and insulin sensitivity.
vial: 10 mg lyophilized; commonly reconstituted in 1 mL to 10 mg/mL
doseRange: 5–10 mg, 2–3 times weekly, or 10 mg once weekly.
evidence: Limited human data; figures are commonly cited research or practitioner use.
disclaimer: Limited human data; figures are commonly cited research or practitioner use.

name: Semax
use: ACTH fragment analogue used for focus and neuroprotection (nasal).
vial: Usually a 0.1% or 1% nasal solution, not a subcutaneous vial
doseRange: 200–600 mcg intranasal, 1–2 times daily, in courses of 5–14 days.
frequency: 1–2 times daily, in short courses of 5–14 days
evidence: Used in Russian clinical practice; limited data in Western trials.
disclaimer: Used in Russian clinical practice; limited data in Western trials.

name: Selank
use: Tuftsin analogue used for anxiety and focus (nasal).
vial: Usually a 0.15% nasal solution, not a subcutaneous vial
doseRange: 250–500 mcg intranasal, 1–2 times daily, in courses of about 10–14 days.
frequency: 1–2 times daily, in courses of about 10–14 days
evidence: Used in Russian clinical practice; limited data in Western trials.
disclaimer: Used in Russian clinical practice; limited data in Western trials.

name: GHK-Cu
use: Copper tripeptide used for skin repair and hair.
vial: 50 mg or 100 mg lyophilized; often 50 mg in 5 mL to 10 mg/mL
doseRange: 1–2 mg daily, or 1–2 mg a few times a week (injectable).
frequency: Daily, or a few times a week
evidence: Most human data are for topical use. Injectable figures are commonly cited research-use.
disclaimer: Most human data are for topical use. Injectable figures are commonly cited research-use.

name: Epithalon
use: Tetrapeptide used in pineal, circadian and ageing-related research.
vial: 10 mg lyophilized; often reconstituted in 1–2 mL
doseRange: 5–10 mg daily for 10–20 days, usually 1–2 courses a year.
frequency: Daily during a 10–20 day course, 1–2 courses a year
evidence: Limited human data (mainly Russian studies); figures are commonly cited research-use.
disclaimer: Limited human data (mainly Russian studies); figures are commonly cited research-use.

name: DSIP
use: Delta sleep-inducing peptide, used for sleep.
vial: 2 mg or 5 mg lyophilized; often 2 mg in 2 mL (1 mg/mL) so 100 mcg is 0.1 mL
doseRange: 25–100 mcg at bedtime, commonly 100 mcg.
evidence: Limited human data; figures are commonly cited research-use.
disclaimer: Limited human data; figures are commonly cited research-use.

name: Sermorelin
use: GHRH analogue used to test and treat growth-hormone deficiency.
vial: 5 mg, 9 mg or 15 mg lyophilized; often 5 mg in 2.5 mL (2 mg/mL) so 200 mcg is 0.1 mL
doseRange: 200–300 mcg subcutaneously at bedtime, daily.
evidence: Previously FDA-approved; figures come from older clinical use (the branded product was withdrawn).
disclaimer: Previously FDA-approved; figures come from older clinical use (the branded product was withdrawn).

name: KPV
use: Alpha-MSH fragment used for gut and skin inflammation.
vial: 5 mg or 10 mg lyophilized; often 5 mg in 2 mL (2.5 mg/mL) so 250 mcg is 0.1 mL
doseRange: 200–500 mcg daily (oral, nasal, or subcutaneous).
evidence: No robust human trial data; figures are commonly cited research-use only.
disclaimer: No robust human trial data; figures are commonly cited research-use only.

name: AOD-9604
use: HGH fragment 176–191, used for fat loss.
vial: 2 mg or 5 mg lyophilized; often 2 mg in 2 mL (1 mg/mL) so 300 mcg is 0.3 mL
doseRange: 250–300 mcg in the morning, or around 300 mcg to 1 mg daily.
frequency: Once daily, often in the morning
evidence: Human trials exist (some did not meet primary weight-loss endpoints). Injectable figures are commonly cited research-use.
disclaimer: Human trials exist (some did not meet primary weight-loss endpoints). Injectable figures are commonly cited research-use.

name: Thymosin Alpha-1
use: Immune-modulating peptide used for hepatitis in some countries.
vial: 1.6 mg vials are the usual clinical size
doseRange: 1.6 mg twice weekly.
evidence: Approved and used clinically in some countries for specific indications (not a general TGA/FDA obesity or wellness approval).
disclaimer: Approved and used clinically in some countries for specific indications (not a general TGA/FDA obesity or wellness approval).

name: PT-141 (bremelanotide)
use: Melanocortin agonist used for hypoactive sexual desire disorder in premenopausal women.
vial: Approved product is 1.75 mg pre-filled; compounded vials are often 10 mg
doseRange: 1.75 mg subcutaneously as needed, no more than one dose in 24 hours.
frequency: As needed, not more than once in 24 hours
evidence: FDA-approved product and dose for a specific indication.
disclaimer: FDA-approved product and dose for a specific indication. A monthly cap applies to the approved product.
